subject: Kickoff: Project Riverbed (DSelect-k for multi-task ranking)
body:
Team,

Kicking off what we're calling Project Riverbed internally — please use the codename in docs and standups so search stays clean.

Substance: our multi-task ranking models currently use softmax-style MoE gating, which is dense (every expert runs) or top-k (non-differentiable selection). DSelect-k from our open-source release gives us differentiable selection of a fixed number of experts — the reference example gates 2 of 4 experts via a DSelectKGate keras layer — so we get sparse inference cost with clean end-to-end training.

Product goal: land DSelect-k gating in the two production multi-task rankers, targeting equal quality at materially lower serving FLOPs.

Milestones: gate layer integrated in the ranker training stack by mid-April, offline A/B quality parity by late May, serving-cost readout before June 15.

Daniela follows up on staffing.

Dmitri
